name: Kora
description_short: A 21-string harp-lute, traditionally played by griots in West Africa.

name: Balafon
description_short: A gourd-resonated xylophone, a precursor to many similar instruments.

name: Djembe
description_short: A rope-tuned, skin-covered goblet drum played with bare hands, originally from West Africa.

name: Talking Drum
description_short: An hourglass-shaped drum whose pitch can be regulated to mimic the tone and prosody of human speech.

name: Goje
description_short: A one or two-stringed fiddle, typically played by the peoples of the Sahel.

name: Shekere
description_short: A percussion instrument consisting of a dried gourd with beads or cowries woven into a net covering the outside.

name: Mbira
description_short: A family of musical instruments, traditional to the Shona people of Zimbabwe, consisting of a wooden board with attached staggered metal tines.

name: Udu
description_short: A plosive aerophone and an idiophone of the Igbo people of Nigeria.

name: Algaita
description_short: A double-reed wind instrument from the Hausa people of West Africa.

name: Nyatiti
description_short: An eight-stringed lyre from Kenya, played by the Luo people.

name: Valiha
description_short: A tube zither from Madagascar made from a species of local bamboo.

name: Inanga
description_short: An oval-shaped trough zither from the Great Lakes region of Africa.

name: Adungu
description_short: An arched harp of the Alur people of northwestern Uganda.

name: Akonting
description_short: A three-string gourd body lute of the Jola people of Senegambia.

name: Bolon
description_short: A traditional Mande string instrument, considered a bass harp-lute.

name: Seperewa
description_short: A 10-14 stringed harp-lute of the Akan and Ashanti people of Ghana.

name: Mvet
description_short: A string instrument, a type of stick zither, of the Fang people of Gabon, Cameroon, and Equatorial Guinea.

name: Krar
description_short: A five or six-stringed bowl-shaped lyre from Ethiopia and Eritrea.

name: Masenqo
description_short: A single-stringed bowed lute commonly found in the musical traditions of Ethiopia and Eritrea.

name: Xalam
description_short: A traditional stringed musical instrument from West Africa, a type of lute.

name: Guembri
description_short: A three stringed skin-covered bass plucked lute used by the Gnawa people.

name: Oud
description_short: A short-neck lute-type, pear-shaped stringed instrument with 11 or 13 strings, common in North Africa.

name: Bendir
description_short: A wooden-framed frame drum of North Africa and the Middle East.

name: Darbuka
description_short: A goblet-shaped hand drum used mostly in North Africa and the Middle East.

name: Gasba
description_short: A type of oblique-rim side-blown flute used in North African music.

name: Kakaki
description_short: A three to four-meter long metal trumpet used in Hausa traditional ceremonial music.

name: Kankobela
description_short: A lamellophone of the Tonga people of Zambia and Zimbabwe, also known as the 'lover's voice'.

name: Kayamba
description_short: A raft rattle made of reeds and filled with seeds, common in Kenya and Tanzania.

name: Oporo
description_short: A long horn blown by the Luo people, used in communication and ceremonies.

name: Sabar
description_short: A traditional drum from Senegal, played with one hand and one stick.

name: Endingidi
description_short: A one-string fiddle popular in the traditional music of Uganda.

name: Uhadi
description_short: A traditional Xhosa musical bow, a stringed instrument with a gourd resonator.

name: Ogene
description_short: A metal bell, usually struck with a soft wooden stick, originating from the Igbo people of Nigeria.

name: Ekwe
description_short: A traditional slit drum made from a hollowed log, used for communication and music by the Igbo people.

name: Gyil
description_short: A gourd-resonated xylophone of the Dagaaba and Lobi people of Ghana, Burkina Faso and Ivory Coast.
